memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Leah saw that she had stopped having children, she took her servant Zilpah and gave her to Jacob as a wife. Leah's servant Zilpah bore Jacob a son. Then Leah said, 'What good fortune!' So she named him Gad. Leah's servant Zilpah bore Jacob a second son. Then Leah said, 'How happy I am! The women will call me happy.' So she named him Asher." - Gen 30:9-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Not to be outdone, Leah answers Rachel's move with the same tactic — she gives her servant Zilpah to Jacob, and two more sons are born. Leah names them with cries of triumph: "What good fortune!" and "How happy I am! The women will call me happy." The competition has fully taken hold of both sisters.

Notice Leah's longing here: "The women will call me happy." She is chasing not only children but the approval and admiration of other people. She wants to be seen as blessed, to win the whispers of the neighbourhood. Much of her striving is aimed at how others will view her.

We can recognise ourselves in this. So often our striving is really about reputation — what people will think, how we will look, whether others will call us successful or happy. But happiness built on the applause of others is fragile and never satisfies for long.

Real, lasting joy is not found in outdoing our neighbours or winning their praise. It is found in God's love and approval, which never changes with the crowd's opinion. Jesus warned against loving human praise more than God's (John 12:43). Seek instead to live before an audience of One. His "well done" is worth more than all the admiration in the world.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How much of my striving is really about what others will think?
2. Am I living for people's applause or for God's approval?
3. Where can I find joy in God rather than in comparison?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, free me from living for the applause of others. Help me to seek Your approval above all, and to find my true and lasting joy in Your unchanging love. Amen.
